newsitem.title: USA: Investigators eye Miami port, Grigsby firm - paper.
newsitem.headline: Investigators eye Miami port, Grigsby firm - paper.

text.p: Federal investigators have opened a probe into Port of Miami Director Carmen Lunetta's relationship with a firm owned by California investment banker Calvin Grigsby, the Miami Herald said Tuesday.
Grigsby, the president of municipal underwriting firm Grigsby & Associates, also owns Fiscal Operations, the firm that manages the gantry cranes at the Port of Miami.

The newspaper said the federal investigators are looking at thousands of dollars in allegedly illegal political contributions, spending on lavish entertainment and perks and payments to Lunetta and former Miami Mayor David Kennedy.
Fiscal Operations provided Lunetta with a leased luxury automobile and $11,000 in cash, the newspaper said. The company also paid $4,000 to Kennedy at Lunetta's direction, the Herald said.

Lunetta abruptly announced his retirement during the weekend, after the Herald reported that seapaort revenues had been spent on questionable expenditures, such as Super Bowl tickets and campaign contributions to Dade County Commissioners. Dade County runs the seaport.
The newspaper said the expenditures were made by Fiscal Operations, often at Lunetta's direction.

Fiscal Operations has a 20-year contract with the port, which calls for it to receive $150,000 a year in management fees, salaries for stevedores and office employees, and expenses. A 1996 audit showed the company billed seaport cargo customers $7.8 million for gantry crane rentals but returned only $1 million to the Port of Miami.
The Herald said internal memos showed Lunetta had considerable control over how much money Fiscal Operations spent before it turned over profits to the seaport.
A Dade County audit revealed last week that the seaport has a $2 million deficit, and Dade Mayor Alex Penelas has requested an outside audit.
Lunetta's resignation takes effect on July 31.
Lunetta was not immediately available for comment.
